title: Household fraud recovery burden varies by age, income, and payment route
source_unit: Weighted US adult SHED 2024 respondents reporting non-credit-card financial fraud or account-involved fraud

denominator.unit: SHED public-use adult respondent rows; conditional outcomes use non-credit-card fraud reporters

other_fraud_exposure_age_18_29.unit: percent of adults in age group

other_fraud_exposure_age_45_59.unit: percent of adults in age group

other_fraud_unrecovered_income_10000_249.unit: percent of other-fraud reporters in income group

other_fraud_unrecovered_income_100000_14.unit: percent of other-fraud reporters in income group

account_fraud_p2p_unrecovered.unit: percent of account-involved other-fraud cases marked P2P with some or all money unrecovered

account_fraud_nonp2p_unrecovered.unit: percent of account-involved other-fraud cases marked non-P2P with some or all money unrecovered

account_fraud_p2p_10_or_more_hours.unit: percent of account-involved other-fraud cases marked P2P

observations.method: Mapped SHED codebook variables BK47_b, BK48, BK50, BK51, and BK52_b to the 2024 public CSV; calculated weighted shares using the 2024 main weight. Age and income condition exposure; loss, unrecovered money, and time condition on the non-credit-card fraud path; account-route comparisons condition on account-involved cases.
observations.uncertainty: No replicate weights or design-based variance fields are available in the public-use file. P2P cells are small and selected; self-report, recall, nonresponse, and survey skip patterns affect estimates.
observations.subgroup: Age, household income, and account-involved fraud by P2P indicator; language and disability were audited but not promoted as general subgroup estimates.
observations.counterinterpretation: The nonmonotonic income pattern and P2P difference may reflect account balances, fraud type, reporting, resources, selection, or payment-provider processes; they do not establish payment-route causation or verified recovery failure.

related_sources.claim: The Federal Reserve publishes the headline fraud, recovery, loss, and time-cost estimates and their source framing.
related_sources.access_boundary: Published tables do not provide all subgroup and route combinations calculated here.

related_sources.claim: Local output records subgroup definitions and weighted calculations.
related_sources.access_boundary: Public-use survey data do not verify provider outcomes or household records.

boundary: This record strengthens the household fraud exposure-to-recovery-burden path with age, income, and account-route conditioning. It does not establish causal payment-route effects, verified firm remedy, digital-access or disability gradients, later trust, switching, or exit.
